audit.whatIsWrong: win[] and phases[].side read Skill/Jayce/Jayce/Skill/Skill/Jayce/Jayce, which contradicts the bespoke whys[] on the same page.
audit.why: whys[0] and whys[1] say you out-range Parrrley and chunk him with the gate-Q, whys[2] calls level 3 a coinflip, and whys[3] through whys[6] say the trade stops going your way, level 6 is a pure danger window, his Sheen spike out-sustains you and he out-scales hard. The chart hands Jayce both item stages the prose says are Gangplank's, and matches the 47.59% win rate over 1641 games only if inverted.
audit.corrected: Jayce / Jayce / Skill / Gangplank / Gangplank / Gangplank / Gangplank.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why and phases[6].why sell Eclipse and the two-item window as your spikes, and loading/breakdown.cooldowns call your R a kill-window ultimate.
audit.why: Jayce's R (Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer) costs no mana on a flat 6-second cooldown - it is a stance swap he uses every rotation, not a saved ultimate. Telling a Jayce player to hoard R for kill windows makes him fight in one form. The item stages belong to Gangplank's Sheen line, which the page's own spikes[3] and late already state.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why and phases[6].why now name his Sheen spike; loading, breakdown.cooldowns and the Common Mistakes report line now describe R correctly as a free 6s swap.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page pairs Remove Scurvy's heal with Grievous Wounds, and Thundering Blow's 20s rank-1 cooldown is never numbered.
audit.why: Remove Scurvy carries the heal flag on a 22/20/18/16/14 cooldown and is the reason your poke does not stick; Grievous Wounds on Serylda's Grudge is the itemisation answer and the page's Itemization line never says so. Thundering Blow is 20/18/16/14/12/10 - at rank 1 spending it on chip leaves you 20 seconds with no way to push him off you.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries the 20s Thundering Blow number and the Itemization report line now ties Serylda's Grievous Wounds to Remove Scurvy.

notes: Jayce's R is not an ultimate in the usual sense: 'No Cost', flat 6s cooldown, pure stance swap with an armour/MR shred on the first cannon-form hit. The generic full-layer template calls it 'the win condition — kill windows only' in loading, breakdown.cooldowns and the Common Mistakes report line. That template text almost certainly repeats across every Jayce matchup, not just this one — worth a global pass. Ability names on this page are all correct; the packet's suspectNames flags for Jayce are false positives.
